source: Times of India report on an IMD/IITM study of India's climate zones, 1951-2020 (lead author Ananya Karmakar)

hot_semi_arid.qualifier: about a quarter of the region's area, grew to a third

temperate.qualifier: shrank from about a quarter to less than a fifth (the article gives no exact later value)

northwest.area_moved_qualifier: roughly 7% of the region moved into the drier zone as temperatures rose and rainfall declined

hot_semi_arid.qualifier: about 30% of the region fell to 16%

peninsula.tropical_savannah_qualifier: now covers about three-quarters of the peninsula, a change the authors attribute to rising rainfall over southern India

places_that_moved.change: the hot, dry zone pushed east into it
moved into the hot semi-arid zone
the tropical monsoon zone extended along them

why_farmers_care: Uttar Pradesh is one of the country's most important farming regions, so the timing of sowing and harvesting needs to be watched closely.
not_reported: The article does not report effects on crop yields or give specific sowing dates.
